study type: Retrospective case series with comparative analysis and literature review
outcome: Severe sequelae (rapid abscess spread, systemic inflammation)
cohort: The study included 3 pregnant and 70 non-pregnant women diagnosed with odontogenic abscesses and treated between January 2020 and April 2025.
finding: Pregnant women with odontogenic abscesses tended to experience more severe sequelae, prolonged intubation, targeted antibiotic use, more extensive surgical interventions, and longer hospitalizations compared to non-pregnant women, although some differences were not statistically significant.
